**English draft for R5 review.**

Here's a trick: when you get pocket money, put some in your piggy bank **first**, before you buy anything. That's called **paying yourself first**.

Even ₹5 a week is great. ₹5 every week for a year is ₹260!

Saving every week, again and again, makes it a **habit**, like brushing your teeth.

Gullak uses virtual play money only.

questions.prompt: You get ₹50. What does "pay yourself first" mean?
questions.explanation: Put some aside as soon as you get it.

questions.prompt: ₹5 every week for 52 weeks adds up to…
Why save a little every week?
questions.explanation: Doing it again and again turns saving into a habit.

variants.markdown:
**English draft for R5 review.**

**Pay yourself first** turns saving from a leftover into a fixed expense: the transfer happens on payday, before discretionary spending. Behavioural research shows that **automation** (a standing instruction or an auto-debit) beats willpower because it removes a monthly decision.

The **savings rate** (saved ÷ income) is a better measure than the amount. Saving ₹3,000 of ₹15,000 is a 20% rate; saving ₹5,000 of ₹1,00,000 is just 5%.

Small regular amounts compound into large ones. ₹1,000 a month for 10 years is ₹1.2 lakh of your own money before any growth. With growth the total is higher, but the rate is an **assumption, not a promise**.

When income rises, raise the savings rate before lifestyle catches up: a simple rule is to save half of every raise. Track streaks, but don't punish a missed month; restarting quickly matters more than a perfect record.

Gullak uses virtual play money only.

questions.prompt: Mira earns ₹15,000 and saves ₹3,000. What is her savings rate?
Why does automating savings on payday tend to work?

options.text: It removes a monthly decision that willpower can lose

questions.explanation: Automation makes saving the default, so it doesn't depend on willpower.

questions.prompt: ₹1,000 a month for 10 years, before any growth, adds up to…
You get a raise. Which habit protects your saving?
questions.explanation: Raising the savings rate with income stops lifestyle creep from eating the raise.
